subject.title: Heartbeat: Use ISO 8601 for Current time and separate trigger timestamp

question: Should heartbeat and cron-style prompt time switch to ISO 8601 local timestamps and expose a distinct heartbeat trigger timestamp, or should the current natural-language local line plus `Reference UTC` remain the model-visible contract?
rationale: The requested change alters shared model-visible prompt semantics and overlaps prompt-cache placement work, so automation should not choose the permanent timestamp contract by itself.

options.title: Adopt ISO plus trigger field
options.body: Update the shared helper and heartbeat wake/runner path to expose machine-readable current and trigger timestamps with focused heartbeat and cron coverage.

options.title: Keep readable current format
options.body: Preserve natural-language local `Current time` plus `Reference UTC` if maintainers prefer current model readability and the existing shipped prompt contract.

options.title: Split heartbeat from cron
options.body: Add heartbeat-specific trigger metadata while leaving cron/system-event current-time formatting unchanged.

recommendation.title: Adopt ISO plus trigger field
recommendation.body: Update the shared helper and heartbeat wake/runner path to expose machine-readable current and trigger timestamps with focused heartbeat and cron coverage.

likelyOwner.reason: This is the strongest current history signal for the shared heartbeat/cron current-time prompt contract.
